props.title: Move Where You Look

B09.capture_spec: C04: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/05-shift-x.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 10.9 s): amount = 0 until 0.52 L, then 0 to 0.25 over 0.52-0.72 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.3, 0.5) stage, (0.9, 0.5) teal, eyes at (0.65, 0.44) and (0.85, 0.44).
B09.visual_intent: Act title 'Move Where You Look' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the shift shader; at right a real Godot window: the teal test sprite sits still while the voice asks which way it will go, then, on 'Watch', slides right inside its square while the readout counts amount 0 to 0.25. A terracotta ring marks the sprite's fixed square.
B09.motion_claim: The picture slides right, clipped by the square's edge, though the code subtracts.

show.event: subtract line highlighted; amount = 0; ring on the fixed square
the slide begins on 'Watch' (video, no cue)
amount = 0.25; the picture is a quarter to the right

B09.runner_up: manim: the window slides over the picture (as B07)
B09.why: A real render of a surprising result (subtract, and it moves right) beats a drawing: the viewer predicts, then sees the real picture move.

B10.visual_intent: Two horizontal rulers from 0 to 1 with ticks at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1: the top one labelled 'the picture' with a teal dot at 0.25, the bottom one labelled 'the shape' with a terracotta pixel marker at 0.5. An arrow runs from the pixel marker up to 0.25 on the picture ruler (tag 'looks up 0.25'), and the teal dot then slides down the arrow to land at 0.5 on the shape ruler (tag 'lands at 0.5').
B10.motion_claim: The pixel at 0.5 reaches back to 0.25, and the teal dot found there lands at 0.5: everything moved a quarter right.

show.event: rulers, ticks, the teal dot at 0.25
pixel marker at 0.5; arrow back to 0.25
the dot lands at 0.5
tag: a quarter right

B10.why: Two rulers with an arrow from 0.5 back to 0.25 turn the worked numbers into motion: the feature slides to where it lands.

B11.visual_intent: Two stacked horizontal rulers as in the previous drawing: the picture (with a teal dot) above, what the shape shows below. First a terracotta arrow pointing right labelled 'subtract from U' with the dot moving right on the lower ruler; then an arrow pointing left labelled 'add to U' with the dot moving left. Persistent small tag: 'the opposite way'.
B11.motion_claim: On 'subtract' the dot moves right; on 'add' it moves left, always against the arrow.

show.event: rulers and dot at rest
subtract: arrow right, dot moves right
add: arrow left, dot moves left

B11.why: Both directions side by side with opposing arrows is the rule itself; the real render of one direction was the previous beats.

B12.capture_spec: C05: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/06-shift-xy.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 10.9 s): shift_y = 0 until 0.36 L, then 0 to 0.25 over 0.36-0.56 L, hold; shift_x = 0 until 0.66 L, then 0 to 0.25 over 0.66-0.86 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Probes (fill-window): shift_y only: eyes cream at (0.4, 0.69) and (0.6, 0.69), (0.4, 0.44) stage; both: eyes at (0.65, 0.69) and (0.85, 0.69).
B12.visual_intent: Code card at left with the two-shift shader; at right a real Godot window where the teal sprite first slides straight down inside its fixed square (shift_y from 0 to 0.25), then also slides right (shift_x from 0 to 0.25), ending right and down. Two readouts count the shifts.
B12.motion_claim: The picture slides down first, then right as well.

show.event: uv -= vec2(shift_x, shift_y) highlighted
the picture slides straight down
it slides right as well: right and down

B12.why: V's downward direction is the surprise; the real sprite sliding down, then right too, shows it on the real picture in the order the voice says it.

B13.capture_spec: C06: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex sprite), lab-shaders/07-scale.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 13.6 s): zoom = 1 until 0.12 L, then 1 to 2 over 0.12-0.45 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state: blob area = 0.2506 of the zoom-1 area (22,865 to 5,731 teal pixels, 640x360 look run), blob centre at (0.25, 0.25) of its square.
B13.visual_intent: Code card at left with the scale shader; at right a real Godot window where the teal sprite shrinks, pinned toward the top left of its fixed square, as zoom grows from 1 to 2. A terracotta ring settles on the top-left quarter of the square (readout 'one quarter'), then on the empty rest (readout 'nothing to read').
B13.motion_claim: The picture shrinks toward the top-left corner and ends in the quarter of its square.

show.event: uv = UV * zoom highlighted
shrinking begins (video)
zoom = 2: the picture fills the top-left quarter
ring on the quarter
ring on the empty rest

B13.why: The picture shrinking into the corner as the dial turns is the claim; the explanation gets its own drawing next (B14).

B14.visual_intent: Two equal-length horizontal rulers: the top one labelled 'the shape' from 0 to 1, the bottom one labelled 'the address' whose scale grows from 0-1 to 0-2 as the dial turns. The first half of the address ruler (0 to 1) is filled teal and labelled 'the picture'; the second half (1 to 2) is grey and labelled 'no picture'. A dashed vertical line joins the middle of the shape ruler to 1 on the address ruler.
B14.motion_claim: The address ruler's labels stretch from 0-1 to 0-2, the teal part is squeezed into the left half and the dashed line lands on 1 at the middle.

show.event: the two rulers, the picture filling the address ruler
the address labels grow to 0-2; teal squeezes to the left half
dashed line from the middle to address 1; 'no picture' on the right half

B14.runner_up: ShaderLab with an address ramp underneath
B14.why: Two rulers (shape position, address) with the picture's extent marked show why only half of each side is filled; a real render shows the shrinking but not the numbers.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · Sprite2D + texture uniform · scripted values

B15.capture_spec: C07: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white) with --tex pic=sprite. Material A (lab-shaders/08-tile-no-repeat.gdshader) until 0.60 L, then --material-at assigns material B (lab-shaders/09-tile.gdshader). Keyframes (L about 12.6 s): zoom = 1 until 0.02 L, then 1 to 2 over 0.02-0.30 L, hold at 2 until 0.72 L, then 2 to 3 over 0.72-0.84 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Probes: no-repeat at zoom 2 shows one blob in the top-left quarter and stage elsewhere; repeat at zoom 3 shows nine teal centres.
B15.visual_intent: Code card at left with the tile shader; at right a real Godot window where the sprite first shrinks alone into the top-left quarter (nothing repeats), then, when the repeat switch comes on, the copies appear at once as a two by two grid and grow to three by three as zoom reaches 3.
B15.motion_claim: The empty space fills with copies the moment repeat switches on.

show.event: default: the lookup returns edge pixels (the quarter stays alone)
repeat enable highlighted
copies appear (material switches)
zoom 3: a three by three grid

B15.runner_up: LectureCodeTrace for the one hint line
B15.why: The switch from no-repeat to repeat in the same render is the event; the copies appear at the moment the voice says the picture starts over.

props.caption: Godot 4.7 documentation · CanvasItem · TextureRepeat · captured at build time

B16.visual_intent: The real Godot 4.7 CanvasItem page scrolled to the TextureRepeat list in a browser window; the camera pushes in on TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED, a terracotta ring marks it, then it moves to TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR. (Ring fractions are estimates: the build sets them from the real capture.)
B16.motion_claim: The camera pushes in on the line the voice names, then moves to the mirror line.

show.event: the page at the TextureRepeat enum
push-in and ring on TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED
ring on TEXTURE_REPEAT_MIRROR

B16.why: The setting is documented API: the real docs page shows the list and its wording; no editor frame is invented.

props.caption: TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game

B17.capture_spec: C08: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex white) with --tex pic=sprite, lab-shaders/10-scroll.gdshader, live TIME, repeat enabled by the shader, zoom fixed by the sprite fit (the picture repeats once per quad width). Render L + 1 s (L about 12.9 s), 30 fps, Forward+. Measured: the picture position under a fixed pixel advances about 0.10 per second (run-3-scroll.log: 0.100 on each of three steps; an earlier run read 0.095 to 0.105).
B17.visual_intent: Code card at left with the scroll shader; at right a real Godot window where the sprite grid slides steadily to the left and wraps around forever. A caption defines TIME (GLOSSARY wording): 'TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game'.
B17.motion_claim: The grid slides left at a steady speed, a tenth of a picture each second.

show.event: uv.x += TIME * 0.1 highlighted
scrolls left, a tenth of its width per second

B17.why: A live TIME scroll is the claim; the code line and the moving picture together.

props.title: Four moves
props.note: Measured in Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · always the opposite of the address

B18.visual_intent: A four-row table, one row ringed as each move is named.
B18.motion_claim: The ring steps down the four rows with the voice.

show.event: subtract row
add row
multiply by more than one row
multiply by less than one row

B18.why: Four parallel move-and-effect facts: the table component is built for exactly that.
